This is a hands-on country leadership role centred on delivery, ownership and readiness for what comes next. The successful candidate will lead the next vitamin A supplementation rounds and post-event coverage surveys, use data to drive corrective action, maintain strong government ownership of the programme, and prepare the team and government partners for the launch of the diarrhoea treatment component in 2027. Deep understanding of Chad’s health system, institutions and communities is a real advantage in this role. Position Nutrition International as a key actor in nutrition and public health through national task forces, alliances and conferences. Engage in advocacy to influence government policy and partner investment in nutrition. Harmonise Nutrition International’s work with other partners and actively support government leadership and ownership. Identify opportunities to leverage and mobilise additional resources to expand Nutrition International’s work in Chad. Programme Management and Delivery Be accountable for achieving agreed results, programme quality and disbursement targets within agreed timelines. Lead delivery of biannual vitamin A supplementation campaigns and post-event coverage surveys. Use survey findings and programme data to identify gaps and drive corrective action. Monitor workplans and performance frameworks and prepare reports for donors and stakeholders. Plan, cost and build government ownership of the 2027 diarrhoea treatment component. Financial Management Ensure country resources are managed in line with Nutrition International policies and within approved budgets. Guide the team in costing, budgeting, expenditure forecasting, variance analysis and value-for-money reporting. Maintain accurate and timely budgets, forecasts and donor reporting. Team Leadership and Country Operations Lead and develop the country team of three Senior Programme Officers and one Project Officer. Set clear roles and performance expectations across the team. Manage country operations, including compliance with legal and financial regulations in Chad. Keep staff informed of programme progress and ensure contributions are recognized. Integrate safety and security considerations into programme design, budgeting, staffing and partner selection. Uphold Nutrition International’s safeguarding standards and code of conduct across the team and partners. At least 10 years of programme or project management experience in public health, nutrition, international development or a related field. A public health or nutrition background. Professional fluency in both English and French. Demonstrable negotiation and stakeholder-navigation skills, particularly with government. Knowledge of Chad; one to two years of in-country exposure is acceptable. Strong delivery discipline and attention to detail, with a track record of using data to drive corrective action. Experience managing complex budgets and diverse teams in progressively senior roles. Clear commitment to safeguarding and to organisational codes of conduct. Desirable Previous experience as a Country Manager, Country Director or Project Director (or equivalent) with an international organisation or NGO. Experience delivering results on large, complex donor-funded programmes, including those supported by USAID or other bilateral and multilateral donors. Experience navigating government ministries and international partners, including WHO and UNICEF. Experience elsewhere in the Sahel or the wider region - for example Nigeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Cameroon or the Republic of Congo. Chadian nationals are strongly encouraged to apply, including Chadian professionals who have built their careers abroad and are ready to return home. Fluency in one or more local languages of Chad. Postgraduate certification in project management, or a certificate in research or monitoring and evaluation.
